name: First time in Akihabara
why: If you are not sure what you like yet, this is the safe and fun one. A shrine at sunset, the famous figure building, hundreds of capsule toys, retro games, an arcade, and the main street lit up at night.
steps: Electric Town exit. A two-minute map of the district.
Anime-themed ema plaques and the shrine from Love Live!, in the last daylight.
Old red-brick railway arches at sunset. The best photo spot of the day.
Floor after floor of figures and goods. See what is popular this month.
Hundreds of capsule toy machines. Pick a souvenir by luck.
Retro games from the 80s and 90s, three floors of them.
One last photo under the neon, then goodbye.
moves: All on foot, about 2.5 km. Short and flat, with breaks inside the shops.
good: First-timers, mixed groups, anyone who wants to see the whole district in one evening.
mind: The sun sets around 16:40 in early November, so we do the outdoor photos first and the neon at the end. Closing times will be re-checked once the date is fixed.

name: Find your favorite
tag: Built around the series you love
why: Tell me the anime or games you love, and we go straight to the shops that have them. New goods first, then the used and rare shops where fans find things they cannot get at home.
steps: New official goods for your series.
Eight floors of used manga, figures and rare items. Real finds, honest prices.
A second shop to dig through. I choose which one by your series.
Look for capsule toys of your favorite characters.
A photo with what you found, under the neon.
moves: All on foot, about 2 km. The shops are close together.
good: Fans with a favorite series or character. Collectors.
mind: Send me the names of the series you love before the day, and I will change the shops and floors to match. The sun sets around 16:40 in early November, so we do the outdoor photos first and the neon at the end. Closing times will be re-checked once the date is fixed.

name: Retro and games
tag: The old electric town and the arcades
why: Akihabara before anime: tiny electronics stalls under the train tracks. Then retro consoles, rhythm games and fighting games, and the arcades at night.
steps: Narrow alleys of electronic parts under the tracks, the way Akihabara started.
Famicom and Super Famicom on the shelves, old arcade machines and Japanese snacks upstairs.
Rhythm games, fighting games, crane games.
A last capsule toy, then a neon photo on Chuo-dori.
good: Gamers, retro fans, people who have seen Akihabara before.
mind: The sun sets around 16:40 in early November, so we do the outdoor photos first and the neon at the end. Closing times will be re-checked once the date is fixed.
